questions.knowledge_point: Finding Points on a Line That Are a Fixed Distance From Another Point on the Line
questions.problem: Consider the straight line that passes through $P(4,0,-1)$ and is parallel to $v=⟨2,-6,3⟩.$ Find all the possible points $A$ on that line such that $PA=7.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find the vector equation of the line, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =p+tv \\ r & =⟨4,0,-1⟩+t⟨2,-6,3⟩\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

Since $A$ lies on the line, we know that there must be a real number $t$ such that

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{OA} & =⟨4,0,-1⟩+t⟨2,-6,3⟩\end{aligned}
$$

and 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PA} & =\overset{\to }{OA}-\overset{\to }{OP} \\  & =(⟨4,0,-1⟩+t⟨2,-6,3⟩)-⟨4,0,-1⟩ \\  & =t\,⟨2,-6,3⟩ \\  & =⟨2t,\,-6t,\,3t⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the fact that $PA=7,$ we get:

$$
\begin{aligned}PA & =7 \\ |\overset{\to }{PA}| & =7 \\ |⟨2t,\,-6t,\,3t⟩| & =7 \\ \sqrt{(2t)^{2}+(-6t)^{2}+(3t)^{2}} & =7 \\ \sqrt{49{t}^{2}} & =7 \\ \pm 7t & =7 \\ t & =\pm 1\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, putting the values $t=\pm 1$ into the equation for the line, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & \overset{\to }{O{A}_{1}}=⟨4,0,-1⟩+⟨2,-6,3⟩=⟨6,-6,2⟩, \\  & \overset{\to }{O{A}_{2}}=⟨4,0,-1⟩-⟨2,-6,3⟩=⟨2,6,-4⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the points are ${A}_{1}(6,-6,2)$ and ${A}_{2}(2,6,-4).$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding a Vector Equation of the Line Passing Through Two Given Points
questions.problem: Find a vector equation of the line that passes through the points $C(-1,0,4)$ and $D(-7,2,11).$
questions.worked_solution:
The vector equation of the straight line passing through $C$ and parallel to $v$ is given by

$$
r=c+tv,
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty )$ and $c$ is the position vector of $C.$ 

We can find a direction vector by computing the displacement vector between the given points $C(-1,0,4)$ and $D(-7,2,11)$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\overset{\to }{CD} \\  & =⟨-7,2,11⟩-⟨-1,0,4⟩ \\  & =⟨-6,2,7⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the vector equation of the line is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0 \\ 4\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ 2 \\ 7\end{aligned}],\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding a Vector Equation of the Line Passing Through Two Given Points
questions.problem: Find a vector equation of the line that passes through the points $F(-5,-2,4)$ and $G(3,-1,1).$
questions.worked_solution:
The vector equation of the straight line passing through $F$ and parallel to $v$ is given by

$$
r=f+tv,
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty )$ and $f$ is the position vector of $F.$ 

We can find a direction vector by computing the displacement vector between the given points $F(-5,-2,4)$ and $G(3,-1,1),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\overset{\to }{FG} \\  & =⟨3,-1,1⟩-⟨-5,-2,4⟩ \\  & =⟨8,1,-3⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the vector equation of the line is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ -2 \\ 4\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}8 \\ 1 \\ -3\end{aligned}],\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Vector Equation of a Line Segment
questions.problem:
The equation below describes all the points on the line segment $\overset{―}{PQ},$ where $P(3,0,-2)$ and $Q(1,1,-1).$

$$
r(t)=[\begin{aligned}a \\ 0 \\ -2\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ b \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,t\in [c,1]
$$

What is the value of $a+b+c?$
questions.worked_solution:
We need to find a direction vector that is parallel to the given line. We can use the vector $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\overset{\to }{PQ} \\  & =\overset{\to }{OQ}-\overset{\to }{OP} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, the vector equation of the line is

$$
r=p+tv\,⟹\,r=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]
$$

and the vector equation of the  line segment $\overset{―}{PQ}$ is

$$
r(t)=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,t\in [0,1].
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
a+b+c=3+1+0=4.
$$

provenance.kp_title: Finding the Vector Equation of a Line Segment

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Vector Equation of a Line Segment
questions.problem:
The equation below gives a parametrization of the line segment $\overset{―}{PQ},$ where $P(3,2,-1)$ and $Q(0,1,-3).$

$$
r(t)=a\,i+b\,j-(2t+1)\,k,\,t\in [0,c]
$$

What is $a+b+c?$
questions.worked_solution:
We need to find a direction vector that is parallel to the given line. We can use the vector $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\overset{\to }{PQ} \\  & =\overset{\to }{OQ}-\overset{\to }{OP} \\  & =(j-3\,k)-(3\,i+2\,j-k) \\  & =-3\,i-j-2\,k\end{aligned}
$$

So, the vector equation of the line is

$$
r=p+tv\,⟹\,r=(3\,i+2\,j-k)+t(-3\,i-j-2\,k)
$$

and the parametrization of the line segment $\overset{―}{PQ}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =(3\,i+2\,j-k)+t(-3\,i-j-2\,k) \\  & =(3-3t)\,i+(2-t)\,j-(2t+1)\,k,\,t\in [0,1].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
a+b+c=(3-3t)+(2-t)+1=6-4t.
$$

provenance.kp_title: Finding the Vector Equation of a Line Segment
